transcript:
Meeting header: date: 2027-06-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes | Attendees: Lydia, Marco, Priya (Redwood); Jared, Alina, Marcus, Nora, Evan (HelioWorks)

Summary (auto): procurement intake & contract redline roadmap; risk items: KMS, data residency, SLA latency/credits; pricing path: pilot -> committed reserved capacity.

00:00:03 Lydia (Redwood): okay everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, um the goal is to map the legal and finance path for a pilot and what a committed deal would look like for HelioWorks. quick intros?
00:00:18 Jared (HelioWorks): Jared, procurement. We run procurement and vendor gating. trying to understand timing for approval and what the blocker list looks like.
00:00:27 Alina (HelioWorks): Alina, security. I'll be triaging SOC 2, data flow diagrams and key management questions.
00:00:33 Marcus (HelioWorks): Marcus, finance — curious about billing cadence and how the committed reserved capacity billing would look.
00:00:40 Nora (HelioWorks): Nora, legal. I'll be looking at MSA/DPA redlines.
00:00:45 Marco (Redwood): Marco here, SE. I'll cover the deployment options, latency profiles, and KMS integrations.
00:00:52 Priya (Redwood): Priya, CSM — I'll own onboarding items and compliance artifacts.

00:01:20 Lydia: Great. Quick context: HelioWorks wants to run a pilot with production-like traffic, likely a mix of hosted API for dev and Dedicated for the production inference lanes. You're looking for clear box pricing and an MSA we can sign. Is that right?
00:01:33 Jared: yeah, pilot then we need internal finance signoff. key is surprises — we need commitments on SLAs and data handling.
00:01:41 Lydia: Understood. Let's go through legal blockers first. Nora, are there must-have clauses you want up front?
00:01:50 Nora: we typically require: standard IP carveouts, limitation of liability caps aligned with our procurement policy, and a DPA that confirms processing only per our instructions plus subprocessor list and data residency commitments. also, if you offer FedRAMP or CJIS reach, mention it.
00:02:08 Lydia: Sure — Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we'll share the attestation. For FedRAMP we don't currently hold FedRAMP, we do support VPC/private deployment and on-prem options for regulated workloads. We'll note that in the MSA.
00:02:20 Alina: KMS — what's supported? customer-managed keys? we require key rotation and no vendor access to plaintext.
00:02:28 Marco: we support customer-managed KMS in our Private deployments and can integrate with customer KMS providers via our KMIP/HSM connectors. For Hosted we have envelope encryption and an option to bring your own key for enterprise tiers, but needs procurement and legal signoff.
00:02:46 Alina: okay that's good to know, we'll want the details in writing.
00:02:53 Marcus: billing — if we move to Dedicated, is it a monthly reserved capacity commit? any ramp credits for the pilot?
00:03:01 Lydia: Dedicated is typically reserved monthly or annual capacity. For pilots we can do a capped pilot invoice or short-term reserved commit — we have internal flex for pilots where we credit some ramping usage into the committed baseline if you convert within 60 days. We'll detail options in the pricing sheet.
00:03:18 Marcus: and billing frequency? net-30? PO process?
00:03:22 Lydia: Net-30 standard; PO accepted. We can do prepay for annual discounts if you prefer.
00:03:30 Nora: on the MSA redlines, do you accept most of our standard procurement language around audit rights and subcontractor flow-downs?
00:03:38 Lydia: we can accept reasonable audit rights, we usually push back only where it conflicts operationally — e.g., constant live access is not feasible but we provide SOC 2 evidence and an on-site or remote audit plan for enterprise customers. Subprocessor flow-downs we maintain and can share a current subprocessor list.
00:03:53 Jared: timeline: procurement typically needs a 2-week legal review, then finance another week. If Redwood can return a clean MSA within 3 business days we can accelerate to a two-week window.
00:04:05 Lydia: okay we'll aim to return annotated MSA/DPA in 3 business days.

00:05:12 Marco: shifting to technical constraints — you mentioned data residency. can you confirm which regions you need, and whether data at rest must remain in-country?
00:05:22 Evan Chu (HelioWorks): For EU and APAC customers, we need at-rest and processing to be within respective regions for PII. For US we have some state-level restrictions but not full separation.
00:05:33 Marco: We can provision Dedicated capacity in EU and APAC regions and ensure KV cache doesn't cross regions for those customers; we'll document the network/VPC layout. There are some caveats with multi-region failover — we'll show the routing policies.
00:05:49 Alina: Do you have a documented runbook for failover and the latencies involved? Security wants RTO/RPO estimates.
00:05:56 Marco: Yes — we have an ops runbook and can give RTOs based on node counts. I'll pull the relevant snippet and add expected tail latencies.

00:06:30 Nora: DPA specifics — can you restrict processing to documented purposes and support data deletion and exports on demand?
00:06:38 Priya: yes we support deletion APIs and export endpoints; we'll include the retention/erasure flow in the DPA annex. We also log deletion requests for audit.
00:06:48 Nora: And what about subprocessor notification windows?
00:06:51 Lydia: standard is 30 days notification for new subprocessors, unless it's a security-critical patch; we can negotiate on enterprise clauses.

00:07:40 Jared: another thing — procurement will need to know the termination for convenience and liability consequences. we have a standard procurement slide deck that outlines acceptable caps.
00:07:48 Lydia: Understandable. We'll highlight our standard liability cap and exceptions for gross negligence. If there's an internal procurement policy doc you can share, we'll map redlines.
00:07:59 Marcus: One more finance question: how are usage overages billed if pilot is on a capped invoice?
00:08:05 Lydia: Overages are typically billed at the overage rates on the invoice; for pilots we can do a true-up with a pre-agreed cap, or include a clause that overage above X% requires an approval. We'll capture options in the pricing sheet.

00:08:40 Marco: technical deep dive note — when comparing hosted vs dedicated cost, the main drivers are token volume, average sequence length, and KV cache hit rates. If you have sample traffic we can model.
00:08:52 Evan (HelioWorks): We can share a week of anonymized telemetry; will that be enough?
00:08:57 Marco: yes, even distribution by endpoint plus sequence lengths will let us recommend quantization profile and batching settings.

00:09:45 Alina: Security: encryption in transit and at rest — is TLS everywhere, cert rotation, and do you have internal HSM?
00:09:52 Marco: TLS everywhere, yes. We use HSM-backed keys for service-level secrets and integrate with customer HSMs for private deployments.
00:10:02 Priya: We'll attach the security whitepaper and cert matrix after the call.

00:10:40 Nora: Another legal nuance — we sometimes require an indemnity for IP infringement only where vendor provides unique models trained on customer data. How does Redwood handle model IP?
00:10:51 Lydia: Redwood serves open models and customer-provided models; we do not claim ownership over customer prompts or outputs. Indemnity requests are rare; we can scope indemnities to vendor-provided proprietary models. We'll mark this as negotiable.

00:11:30 Jared: competitors — procurement will likely ask if we considered Anthropic or OpenAI; be transparent on differentiators.
00:11:36 Lydia: Sure — we position on predictable inference economics and private deployment options; we'll include a short competitive note.

00:12:02 Marco: For the pilot, recommended setup: provision a small dedicated pool for production traffic, and use hosted dev tokens for dev. Then run a 2-week benchmark comparing latency P50/P95 and tail tail. We'll provide the benchmark scripts.
00:12:16 Marcus: That helps with the finance case. If the pilot proves out, finance prefers to do an annual commit for discounting.
00:12:22 Lydia: we can show delta between monthly reserved and annual prepay.

00:13:10 Priya: Onboarding timeline — once MSA signed, typical lead time to stand up a small Dedicated pool is 2-3 weeks depending on region. For Private on-prem it's longer.
00:13:20 Evan: Two to three weeks is acceptable. We need to align on maintenance windows and planned downtimes.
00:13:26 Marco: We'll commit to scheduled maintenance windows and a change management calendar as part of the SLA annex.

00:14:05 Nora: One more: can you support SSO with SAML + SCIM provisioning?
00:14:10 Lydia: yes SAML SSO is supported, SCIM for user provisioning is available on enterprise plans. We'll send setup docs.

00:14:40 Jared: Given procurement cycles, Jason from our executive team may want to see the pricing path for committed capacity — can we get a one-pager with pilot pricing + conversion discounts?
00:14:51 Lydia: Absolutely — we'll include conversion credit language so you can show net-cost if you convert to committed.

00:15:30 Marcus: curious about SLA credits for latency — do you offer service credits or financial penalties?
00:15:36 Marco: We provide SLA credits tied to uptime and API availability; latency SLOs are documented per model type and region; financial penalties are rare but credits are standard. We'll include the SLA matrix.

00:16:12 Alina: encryption key access — we need a statement that Redwood personnel cannot decrypt customer data without an emergency process.
00:16:20 Priya: We'll add the emergency access process and approval matrix into the security annex; it's tracked in audit logs.

00:17:00 Lydia: OK let's talk about next steps timeline. We'll send annotated MSA/DPA in 3 business days and include SOC 2, security whitepaper, performance spreadsheet and a pricing one-pager. Marco will add the dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoff.
00:17:14 Nora: We'll aim to do an internal legal pass within two weeks of receiving your annotated MSA. Procurement will follow and finance will review pricing the week after.
00:17:25 Jared: If we can close legal in 2 weeks and finance in 1 week after that, we could sign by early July. that's our optimistic timeline.

00:18:10 Marco: just to capture a small technical ask — Evan please share the telemetry sample with sequence lengths and a rough split of LLM vs embedding calls. That will let us size the KV cache and batching.
00:18:22 Evan: will do, forward by 2027-06-17.
00:18:30 Lydia: Great — I'll follow up with an email summarizing action items and attach the MSA template.

00:19:00 Brief pause, cross talk, logistics about timezones and next meeting scheduling.

00:23:05 Nora: small question — do you accept GDPR data subject requests within 30 days?
00:23:10 Priya: Yes, we commit to 30-day response per the DPA; export and deletion APIs will be part of the annex.

00:24:40 Marcus: finance asks whether discounts apply to overage rates if we exceed committed baseline by more than 20%?
00:24:48 Lydia: We can tier overage rates; beyond 20% we'll propose a temporary elevated rate pending review, but conversion to a larger commit is usually the cost-effective path.

00:26:00 Jared: any blockers we haven't covered?
00:26:03 Alina: need the KMS connector docs and proof of no plaintext access for hosted.
00:26:08 Lydia: We'll provide that.
00:26:15 Nora: I'll send the procurement playbook with must-haves for contracts.

00:30:00 Lydia: Ok let's recap — action list and owners, Redwood sends annotated MSA/DPA, security artifacts, pricing one-pager, and benchmark template. HelioWorks shares telemetry sample and procurement playbook. We'll reconvene after the first legal pass.
00:30:15 Jared: agreed. Thanks everyone.
00:30:20 Lydia: Thanks, we'll follow up with dates.

00:31:00 End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional filler words removed, some speaker labels normalized. There are a few minor mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed consistently but sometimes spelled as "K-V cache").

Attachments referenced: MSA_template_v2.docx (sent post-call), Redwood_Security_Whitepaper.pdf (link to share), Pricing_OnePager.xlsx, Dedicated_vs_Hosted_Benchmark_Template.csv
